title: Kenji's treat
setting: An evening voicemail. Okaasan calls Yuki to tell her about going out for ramen with Kenji, who has just been paid for his part-time job, and to invite her along on Saturday.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.ja: もしもし、ユキ？お母さんだけど。
lines.kana: もしもし、ゆき？おかあさんだけど。

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kyou ne, kenji to gohan itte kita no.
lines.ja: 今日ね、ケンジとご飯行ってきたの。
lines.kana: きょうね、けんじとごはんいってきたの。
lines.english: Kenji and I went out to eat today.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji ga ne, baito no okane ga haitta kara, kyou wa ogoru yo tte.
lines.ja: ケンジがね、「バイトのお金が入ったから、今日はおごるよ」って。
lines.kana: けんじがね、「ばいとのおかねがはいったから、きょうはおごるよ」って。
lines.english: Kenji goes, 'My part-time pay just came in, so today's on me.'

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji no suki na raamen no mise ni itta n da kedo, sugoku kondete ne.
lines.ja: ケンジの好きなラーメンの店に行ったんだけど、すごく混んでてね。
lines.kana: けんじのすきならーめんのみせにいったんだけど、すごくこんでてね。
lines.english: We went to Kenji's favourite ramen place, but it was absolutely packed.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.kana: さんじゅっぷんもはいれなかったのよ。
lines.english: We couldn't get in for a whole half hour!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: de, ryou ga sugoku ooi no. okaasan, hanbun shika taberarenakatta.
lines.ja: で、量がすごく多いの。お母さん、半分しか食べられなかった。
lines.kana: で、りょうがすごくおおいの。おかあさん、はんぶんしかたべられなかった。
lines.english: And the portions are huge. I could only eat half of mine.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: demo kenji wa, mada onaka suiteru tte, mou ippai tanonda no yo.
lines.ja: でもケンジは、「まだおなかすいてる」って、もう一杯頼んだのよ。
lines.kana: でもけんじは、「まだおなかすいてる」って、もういっぱいたのんだのよ。
lines.english: But Kenji said he was still hungry and ordered another bowl!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sore de ne, kenji ga are? okane tarinai tte.
lines.ja: それでね、ケンジが「あれ？お金足りない」って。
lines.kana: それでね、けんじが「あれ？おかねたりない」って。
lines.english: And then Kenji goes, 'Huh? I don't have enough money.'

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: dakara, okaasan ga ogotchatta. ogotte moraeru to omotta noni!
lines.ja: だから、お母さんがおごっちゃった。おごってもらえると思ったのに！
lines.kana: だから、おかあさんがおごっちゃった。おごってもらえるとおもったのに！
lines.english: So I ended up paying for us both. And there I was thinking I'd get a treat!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: doyoubi, yuki mo gohan ikanai? kenji ga, kondo wa honto ni ogoru tte.
lines.ja: 土曜日、ユキもご飯行かない？ケンジが、今度はほんとにおごるって。
lines.kana: どようび、ゆきもごはんいかない？けんじが、こんどはほんとにおごるって。
lines.english: Want to come out to eat with us on Saturday, Yuki? Kenji says this time it's really on him.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ano mise, yoru wa komu kara, ohiru ni ikou ne. ohiru mo aiteru kara.
lines.ja: あの店、夜は混むから、お昼に行こうね。お昼も開いてるから。
lines.kana: あのみせ、よるはこむから、おひるにいこうね。おひるもあいてるから。
lines.english: That place gets packed in the evenings, so let's go at lunchtime. It's open at lunch too.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ryou ga ooi kara, onaka sukasete kite ne. jaa ne, oyasumi.
lines.ja: 量が多いから、おなかすかせてきてね。じゃあね、おやすみ。
lines.kana: りょうがおおいから、おなかすかせてきてね。じゃあね、おやすみ。
lines.english: The portions are big, so come hungry. Okay, bye. Good night.

questions.english: What happened when Okaasan and Kenji went out to eat?

choices.english: The ramen place was so packed that they gave up and went home, so she wants to try again with Yuki at lunchtime on Saturday.
Kenji said the meal was on him, but after ordering a second bowl he was short of money, so she ended up paying.
She took Kenji out for ramen to celebrate his first pay, but the portions were so big that neither of them could finish.

questions.explanation: Line 3: Kenji's part-time pay has come in, so he says kyou wa ogoru yo (today's on me). Line 7: still hungry, he orders another bowl (mou ippai tanonda). Line 8: he's short of money (okane tarinai). Line 9: okaasan ga ogotchatta, so Mom ended up paying, after thinking she'd be the one treated (ogotte moraeru to omotta noni). A is wrong: sanjuppun mo hairenakatta (line 5) means they couldn't get in for half an hour, not that they gave up; they got in and ate (lines 6-7). Saturday lunch is because the place gets packed in the evenings (line 11). C is wrong: it was Kenji who offered to pay (line 3), and only Mom couldn't finish (line 6: hanbun shika taberarenakatta). Kenji was still hungry and ordered more (line 7).

questions.english: It's Saturday, a little before noon, and you're at your mother's. She sighs, "aa, onaka suita." (Oh, I'm hungry.) Suggest going out to eat.
questions.answer: Suggest it with gohan and iku, no taberu needed: jaa, gohan ikou! or ne, gohan ikanai?

modelAnswers.english: Then let's go out and eat!
Hey, want to go get some food?

questions.explanation: gohan ni iku is the everyday way to say 'go out to eat'. It needs no taberu, and casual speech drops ni: gohan ikou (let's go eat) or gohan ikanai? (want to go eat?), the way Okaasan invites Yuki in line 10 (doyoubi, yuki mo gohan ikanai?). Line 2 is the past: kenji to gohan itte kita (Kenji and I went out to eat). Spelling it all out as yuushoku o tabe ni ikou sounds stiff, and resutoran ni ikou points to a Western-style restaurant.

questions.english: Planning Saturday, Okaasan says "ano mise, yoru wa komu kara, ohiru ni ikou ne." Why does she want to go at lunchtime?
questions.ja: お母さんは、なんでお昼に行きたいんですか？
questions.kana: おかあさんは、なんでおひるにいきたいんですか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa, nande ohiru ni ikitai n desu ka?

choices.english: The place is closed in the evenings.
The portions are smaller at lunchtime.
The place gets packed in the evenings.

questions.explanation: Line 11: ano mise, yoru wa komu kara. Plain komu means 'gets crowded', what tends to happen. konderu means 'is packed' at a given moment, as in line 4 (sugoku kondete ne), when they couldn't get in for half an hour (line 5). A mixes komu up with aku: aiteru means 'is open', and Okaasan says ohiru mo aiteru kara (it's open at lunch too). The place was open when they went, just full. B is wrong: the portions come up in line 12, ryou ga ooi kara, onaka sukasete kite ne (they're big, so come hungry), and nothing is said about smaller lunch servings.

questions.english: Kenji had just been paid for his part-time job. What did he say to his mother?
questions.ja: ケンジくんは、お母さんに何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじくんは、おかあさんになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-kun wa, okaasan ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Today I'll buy you some food.
choices.romaji: kyou wa gohan katte ageru yo.

questions.explanation: Line 3: baito no okane ga haitta kara, kyou wa ogoru yo. ogoru is the payer's verb, like 'treat', so Kenji, the one with money, says ogoru. B, ogotte morau, is said by the person being treated. It's what Okaasan expected for herself in line 9 (ogotte moraeru to omotta noni!), and from Kenji it would mean he expected her to pay. C is 'I'll buy you dinner' word for word: gohan o katte ageru sounds like buying her some food to take home, like a bento, not paying for a meal out.

questions.english: You and your mother are at the ramen place. She sees you've only eaten half your bowl and asks, "e, hanbun shika tabetenai no?" (What, you've only eaten half?) Tell her it's a huge portion.
questions.ja: え、半分しか食べてないの？
questions.kana: え、はんぶんしかたべてないの？
questions.answer: Explain with ryou ga ooi, not ookii: datte, ryou ga sugoku ooi n da yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: datte, ryou ga sugoku ooi n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: だって、量がすごく多いんだよ。

modelAnswers.romaji: koko, ryou ooi ne. mou onaka ippai.
modelAnswers.ja: ここ、量多いね。もうおなかいっぱい。
modelAnswers.english: The portions here are big, huh. I'm already full.

questions.explanation: An amount of food is ooi (a lot) or sukunai (not much): ryou ga ooi, as Okaasan says in line 6 (ryou ga sugoku ooi no) and line 12 (ryou ga ooi kara). ookii is the size of a thing (ookii sara, a big plate), so 'ryou ga ookii' sounds wrong. Casual speech often drops ga (koko, ryou ooi ne), and datte ... n da yo gives the reason you stopped eating.

newWords.english: part-time job (baito no okane = pay from a part-time job)
one bowl or glass (mou ippai tanonda = ordered another bowl); not the ippai of onaka ippai (full)
this time; next time (kondo wa = this time)
